text:
Theo’s quiet contemplation of the night sky was not merely a pastime but a sacred ritual inherited from his mother, an astrophysicist whose passion for the cosmos had been passed down to him like a precious heirloom. Her absence left a void that the stars seemed to fill, offering him a sense of continuity and connection to the universe she loved so dearly. As he gazed upward, he often imagined her voice guiding him through the constellations, turning the cold vacuum of space into a warm, familiar embrace. This deep-seated bond fueled his determination to understand the heavens, driving him to pursue a career in astronomy despite the challenges he faced.

In the distance, fluffy things in the sky rain comes from, drifting lazily across the twilight like cotton candy spun by the wind. These soft, white clouds seemed to echo the gentle nature of his mother’s teachings, reminding him that even the heaviest storms are preceded by moments of serene beauty. Theo found comfort in this duality, knowing that just as rain nourishes the earth, the memories of his mother continued to sustain his spirit. His fascination with the stars was thus intertwined with a profound appreciation for the cycles of nature, each element playing its part in the grand tapestry of life.
